To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
clear-cutting and soil treatment increase the export of nitrogen, phosphorus, and suspended solids from forested catchments for a long time (10-14 years).

clear-cutting and soil site preparation can increase the annual export of total nitrogen, total organic nitrogen, ammonium, nitrate, total phosphorus, phosphate, total organic carbon, suspended solids and runoff from boreal forested catchments for more than 10 years after the treatment, and that these increases are only statistically significant when the area affected is more than 30 % of the catchment area.

clear cutting and soil preparation in boreal forests can cause significant increases in the export of N and P, and SS, for many years after clear cutting, and that the increases are only large when the area of forest harvesting exceeds 30 % (or more) of catchment area.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the impacts of clear-cutting on the export of nitrogen and phosphorus from catchments in Eastern Finland and the long-term effects are discussed in the context of current European Union (EU) legislation.
the long-term impacts of forest management practices on surface water quality and the export of nutrients from catchments in the boreal zone.
the long-term effects that forest clear-cutting and soil scarification have on the export of nutrients and SS from borean catchments.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the current clear-cutting and soil treatment methods in boreal catchments do not increase the export of nitrogen and phosphorus to surface water, and that the increase in SS export is small.

the impacts of clear-cutting on surface water quality can be minimized by keeping the proportion of clear-cutting to the area of a catchment below 30 % and by leaving wide buffer zones along the streams.
the impacts of forest management practices on surface water quality are small, at least in the long term.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the current forest management practices in Finland have a limited effect on water quality.
clear cutting and soil preparation can increase the export from boreal catchment of N, P, and SS for many years (> 10 years), but only when the area of treatment exceeds 30 %.
the impacts on water quality are not very large in the long run.
The main takeaway from our work is that

current forest management practices have the potential to significantly increase the export of total N, NO3-N and PO4-P from boreal catchment, but the effects are only significant when a large proportion of the catchment is affected.
the effects of clear-cut harvesting on water quality can be mitigated by leaving wide buffer zones along streams and rivers.
the long-term impact of forest management practices on surface water quality is largely dependent on catchment area and the size of the clear-cut area.
